[II 135] The Occult Properties of Certain Surahs the Glorious Occult Properties of Surat Al-Fātiḥa Surat al-Fātiḥa possesses many glorious occult properties (khawāṣṣ, occult properties) and wondrous secrets. Our master the Prophet, Muḥammad al-Mustafa, God's blessings and peace be upon him, has said of Surat al-Fātiḥa:
Ummul Kurāni shifāun min kulli dāin (The Mother of the Qur'an — the Fātiḥa — is a cure for every ailment.)

Among the surahs of the Noble Qur'an, the Fātiḥa is the surah without the letter Fe, and it protects against every calamity. Our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad, God's blessings and peace be upon him, has also said of Surat al-Fātiḥa:
zeteyni fekad emine kulli shayʾin illel mevt.
(Whoever recites the Fātiḥa before sleeping, together with Surat al-Ikhlāṣand the two Surahs of Refuge, is safe and protected from everything except death.)
Our master the Prophet said: the Fātiḥa is a cure for everything except sām — and sām is death.
The Fātiḥa is undoubtedly a remedy for seventy ailments. It heals sickness and pain and hastens recovery, and this holds whether it is recited or written.
Surat al-Fātiḥa consists of 124 letters, and its total abjad (numerical alphabet) value is 9361.

1. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, has related: one day Hasan ibn Ali fell ill. Our master the Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad, God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: let the noble Fātiḥa — the surah revealed without the letter Fe — be recited forty times over a bowl of water. Let Hasan then wash his hands, feet, face, head, and his entire body with that water. God Almighty will grant him healing from every affliction and illness.

3. Hazreti Ali, may God ennoble his countenance, has said: whoever recites Surat al-Fātiḥa once a day in the arrangement (tertip) given below will attain his desires in this world and the next. God Almighty will make the hearts of others submit to the one who recites it, and will lift every calamity from him.
Sheikh Muhyiddin ibn Arabi, may God be pleased with him, has said:

whoever recites Surat al-Fātiḥa in its arranged form seven (7) times daily will behold the world of the unseen, hidden and veiled from ordinary people. He will gain insight into the spirits of the Kingdom and establish contact with the world of Compulsion. He will break free from the lower world and forge a complete bond with the world of eternal subsistence. He will attain his aims in this world and the next and reach the path of victory. Through God Almighty's grace and favor, he will become master of these secrets.

The manner of reciting is as follows: in a place where no one is present, with body and clothing clean, perform a thorough ablution, then pray two rak'ahs of the Prayer of Need. After the prayer, seek forgiveness seventy times, and send blessings upon our Prophet, Hazreti Muḥammad, God's blessings and peace be upon him, seventy times. Then recite the arrangement of the Fātiḥa given below seventy times, and whatever your need [II 137] may be, ask it of God Almighty. Without doubt, God will grant the reciter's need that very day — perhaps even within that very hour. Many doors of the heart and of hidden secrets will be opened to the one who recites it. God Almighty, through His grace and generosity, will make the reciter wealthy.

The noble Bukhari, may God be pleased with him, says: whoever recites Surat al-Fātiḥa in this arrangement seven times daily will need no one for his worldly needs, and God Almighty will open to him the doors of the unseen.

Each of the seven verses of the Fātiḥa has been set to correspond to one day of the week. Together with the spirits of the higher and lower worlds that hold sway on those days, the names and letters of the days have also been assigned to them.

9. If you wish to obtain the servant spirits (khuddām) of Surat al-Fātiḥa: fast for three days in ascetic discipline (riyada). Each day recite Surat al-Fātiḥa 1000 times together with the invocation below. While reciting, burn storax, coriander, and male frankincense as incense. By the end of the third day you will obtain the servant spirits of Surat al-Fātiḥa. The servant spirit (khadim) of Surat al-Fātiḥa is the angel Uhaydar, and his assisting servant is Reyhan. With the servant spirit of Surat al-Fātiḥa you may exercise power (taṣarruf) for good or for ill.

[II 168] The Sublime Occult Properties (khawāṣṣ) of Surah Ya-sin The blessing and virtue of this noble surah are manifest, and its effects are abundant in every respect. Many noble hadiths have been related on this subject. In a hadith related from Enes bin Malik, our Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings upon him) said as follows:
(Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin.)

Likewise, our master the Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings upon him) said to Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him): "O Ali! I recommend Ya-Sin to you. For the one who recites it there are twenty blessings." Among these: if a hungry person recites it, he is satisfied; if a thirsty person recites it, his thirst is relieved; if a naked person recites it, he is clothed; if an unmarried person recites it, he marries; if a fearful person recites it, he is freed from his fears; if a sick person recites it, he attains healing; if a prisoner recites it, he is released; if a traveler recites it, he arrives safely at his destination; if one who has lost his way recites it, he finds his way; if a troubled person recites it, Allah Most High lightens his trouble; and if someone whose belongings are lost or stolen recites it, by the leave of Allah, Glorious and Exalted, he finds his belongings. If it is recited over a dead person, his state is surely eased.

In another noble hadith it is said: "Ya-Sin is for whatever purpose it is recited; whatever the intention behind its recitation, it has an effect upon that matter. The past and future sins of the one who recites Surah Ya-Sin are forgiven. The divine mysteries within the noble Qur'an lie within the noble Ya-Sin." These noble hadiths show that the noble Ya-Sin is a great treasure whose sublime occult properties (khawāṣṣ) exert their effect in every matter, both of this world and the next.

Merciful, the Compassionate. "Peace" — a word from a Merciful Lord.) This is verse 58, and it is made up of sixteen letters and four words. Of the sixteen letters, seven occur once and nine are repeated. The letters occurring once are Sin, Qāf, Wāw, Nun, Be, Ha, and Ye. Of the repeated letters, Alif occurs twice, Lam twice, Ra twice, and Mīm three times. The letters occurring once — sin, qāf, wāw, nun, be, ha, and ye — correspond to the seven planets, while the repeated letters alif, lam, ra, and mīm correspond to the nine celestial spheres. This verse contains six dots in all: three above, on the Qāf and Nun, and three below, on the Be and Ye. The two dots of the Qāf relate to fire and air; the two dots of the Ye relate to earth and water. The dot of the Nun relates to the sun, and the dot of the Be relates to the moon. The letters of this verse likewise embody the four elements: there are five letters of fire, four of earth, two of air, and five of water. The abjad (the numerical alphabet) value of this verse, taken as a sum, is 818.

Before beginning to recite this verse, one should start Surah Yā-Sīn from the beginning and, on reaching this verse, recite it 818 times, then continue reading the sūrah to its end; doing so hastens the expected benefit.

(Everything has a light, and the light of the Qur'an is "Say: He is Allah, the One")

Again, concerning Sura Al-Ikhlāṣour master, peace and blessings be upon him, said the following: whoever recites "Kulhuwallāhu Ehad" [i.e., Sura Al-Ikhlāṣ, so named from its opening words] once is as if he had recited a third of the noble Qur'an.
Whoever recites Kulhuwallāhu Ehad three (3) times is as if he had recited the entire noble Qur'an.
Whoever! recites Kulhuwallāhu Ehad ten (10) times — Allah, glorious and exalted is He, builds him a house in Paradise for it.
Whoever! recites Kulhuwallāhu Ehad fifty (50) times — Allah forgives him fifty years' worth of sins, excepting debts owed to other people and the gravest sins.
Whoever! recites Kulhuwallāhu Ehad one hundred times, whether within the ritual prayer or outside it — Allah Almighty writes him a certificate of deliverance from Hell.

Treatments for the Illness of Epilepsy and Jinn-possession Epilepsy
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 267
Epilepsy is a cold and malignant humor concealed within the human body. Settling especially in the cavities of the brain, it is a grave illness, also called junūn (madness).

This illness of epilepsy is not always quiet; it grows more severe in rainy, cloudy, windy, and cold weather. Epilepsy begins in the feet and rises up to the brain. When it reaches the brain, the seizure takes hold of the patient, and if he happens to be standing at that moment, he falls to the ground. The patient senses this and strives not to fall, but he has not the strength [II 268] for it. Some epileptics, the instant they feel the seizure coming on, want to cover themselves at once, because their mental balance has been disturbed. You will see him speaking and answering without any awareness.

The treatment for this illness: the epileptic is kept in a house with clean air and no draft. You anoint the patient's head and entire body with a liquid oil. If he is fed rich, fatty and meaty foods of a moist and warm nature — such as walnuts, ewe's milk, clotted cream, butter, poultry meat, egg yolk, dried and fresh grapes, dates, bananas, and sweet pomegranate — and kept away from all other foods, the patient recovers, by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

Burning Jinn with Medicines and Herbs
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 283

1. If you wish to burn jinn with medicines, to treat with snuff and papers, and to overpower the afflicting jinn: take a quantity of meyatus sāile (a flowing aromatic resin), the same quantity of haltit (asafoetida), as much uzerlik (wild rue) as the two combined, as much sedef otu (rue) as the three combined, as much hanzal (colocynth) as the four combined, and as much [II 284] dried pomegranate rind as the five combined. Take all of these and pound them until soft, until they turn into something like flour. Add sharp vinegar to the mixture and work it into a paste. Put this paste into a bottle, bury it in warm manure, and leave it for forty days. After forty days the preparation inside the bottle turns into a cream. On the forty-first day, take the bottle out of the manure, add a little garlic to it, and mix well. If you wish to overpower the jinn and drive it out of the body, expelling it, drip a little of this mixture into the possessed patient's nose, and rub some of it over the patient's body as well. If you smear some of this cream onto a piece of paper, burn the paper, and have the patient inhale its smoke through the nose, the jinn will burn and, by the permission of Allah, glory be to Him, never return to that body again.

This working is even stronger and more effective against ferezdak, falic (paralysis), and hirab (names of nervous ailments). You will overcome these diseases, and torment the jinn afflicting the possessed, only by means of these burning names and medicines.

If a person fumigates his clothing with this cream (bakhūr — that is, perfumes it with smoke), no jinn will have the power to overcome him until he washes that clothing. That completes the treatment — after, of course, the prayers, the incantations, the recitations, and the fumigations have been carried out.

On the tenth and twentieth days, add a little olive oil into the bottle. On the twenty-first day this mixture becomes like tar. Take the bottle out of the manure, knead the preparation inside it with garlic juice, put it back into a glass bottle, and store the bottle carefully. When you wish to burn the jinn of a possessed patient, drip a little into the patient's nose and ear, and rub the patient's body with this ointment as well; by the permission of Allah, glory be to Him, the jinn will come forth and burn.
